title: Dad in Mexico, Piron riverboat trip, lake boat job and Cornelius's guitar
summary: More on Dad, then his trip on the steamer with Piron's band, leaving the boat, the Pontchartrain boat job, and Cornelius's head through a guitar.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: Yeah, and I finished talking about little Dad. Yeah, I finished that too. I finished talking about little Dad and Cornish. So, Cornish used to kid Dad, you know, all the time. Well Dad's a little bit of a fellow, you know, he'd say, I'm a man boy. He'd say, but I'm a small man. But I got plenty of brains out of him. I got plenty of brains out of him. And he'd go and he'd start, oh, you know, he wasn't fighting, but Cornish would be playing with him, you know. But he'd be juicing, he thought, you know. He'd start hitting that Cornish and Cornish would hit at him like that, you know, and he'd run through, Dad would run through Cornish's leg. And Octave told me that Dad went out to, when he took Dad to Mexico, you know, little Dad, Octave told me, Crosby told me, I said, took Dad to Mexico, saying, you know, Octave doesn't drink, you know, he ain't drink anything, saying, Dad went out and got full of the Mexican, you know, Chiquilla, you know what it was called. He said, Dad come down the road hooping. Whoop! He said, I done killed 40 Mexicans and I killed them. He said, I think, grand, he said, come here boy. He said, those people can throw a knife and block you. So, yeah, so I mean, I ended up, I happened to play with another band I went with, I'll tell you, the band I went with was P-Run, AJ P-Run's band. I played with them, I made a trip with them on the boat, on the steam jazz, but we had to get off there in St. Louis and play on the President also, you know, because there were two bands and, well, I went up there with them, we had a trip up there, the band was consisted of myself, Joe Phillips, Eddie Pearson playing Tramon, P-Jone, well P-Jone led the band, he did all the, mostly the band, the first band, P-Jone did most of the leading, and Manuel Sells, the late Boecker, Washington, and let's see who else named, Arthur Durabney, and what was the brother, Ruzon I think it was playing, Ruzon, and John Kazma's brother, Bill, playing tenor. Let's see, I believe that's all, yeah, we had Louis Barber and playing drums, Louis Barber and playing drums, that band, he had a fine band at that time. I took Leo Dajon to play at that time, you know, and went up for us, so Joe Phillips said, when I went up there, because Leo Dajon plays a much different mind, you know, my style was different from him, you know, but when I first went on the boat, the captain didn't like my playing, you know, like, because Leo had such a, and it's true a fella, you know, if you're used to listening to that trumpet, it'd be different, you know, so after I went on the boat and stayed up there, we got there, so Joe Phillips said, man, he said, if you're going to get to Memphis, Tennessee, if you have your trumpet there and your uniform, say you done got cap, you know. I said, yeah, so when we got to Memphis, Tennessee, the uniforms and the trumpet and everything was there for me, you know. I know after I left there, somewhere around, I didn't like the boat, you know, for some reason, after I hadn't gone that far, you know, all the fellas liked it, but I mean, it was kind of rough, you know, you play all evening and then you got to play at night too, you know, you play those picnics or those. Sometimes a day, clock in the morning, picnics all day, you know, and you play in the evening. So when we got to them, where I got to, I told Peter that I want to leave, you know, so they asked me to stay two more weeks. If I stay two more weeks, he'll give them my fare back. So I decided to stay two more weeks, two more weeks. Well, after that, he couldn't get nobody to come, you know. So he sent for Pajou, I believe. But Pajou hadn't come, though, when I left. Joe Phillips had to play for his trumpet. So Joe Phillips had to play for his trumpet, see. So, we went down to, people went down to talk to him, brought me down to talk to him, and he's asking me to stay, you know. So he said, well, you got to forget about what I said and what I thought. I told him, I said, well, it wasn't that a fella, but I said, well, I got an interest in the band, because we had a band, Celestine Band, it was a band, you know, it was a company band, you know. And you had stock, like you bought all those automobiles, you know, and all the things, well, you lose that, you know, if you stay away from the band, you know. So I tell him, I said, no, I have interest in the band, I'm playing with Tuxi, the band, I said, I've been playing with them, and I decided to go back, go back with the band, you know. He said, well, no, he said, you look like you're angry, because I said, well, I said, let me tell you one thing. He said, I fired Lil Armstrong on this boo. He said, look where he's at. I said, well, I fired Lil Armstrong, he said, and about me saying anything about you. He said, I found out after you got up here, he said, now when you go down the ass, I didn't know. He said, but I found out after you got up, since you had, you been up here around these people, saying, those people are crazy about the band, so you got, in that time, I had a band, you know, say, you got a Benny Goodman band, one of the greatest swing bands, you know, ever come up the rim. So then Fat Fischer got angry with him, he and Fat, I mean, he and Fess had some words about it, so Fess got asked me to interfere in the band, so Fess thought I was angry too about it, but I wasn't, you know. Really, I came on back home, I just want to come back, you know. So I left the boat in Denport, Iowa, and went to Chicago and stayed there. My uncle offered me a place to stay free a month. I should have stayed, I don't know, but he loved New Orleans, but the South I came over here, he said, I'm going to give you a place to stay and feed you a month, and if you don't get a break in that time, you can go back home. I don't know, just love, New Orleans. I came on back home, see, and never did go back anymore. And I played on this. This boat go across, these guys, I was taking a camellia. I used to play on that plencher boat running across Lake Pontius Rang, you know. I played on that regla, me and Ruben Hughes, and Ruben McClennis, Lil Bob, he's dead, like Bob Davis, Jim Davis' brother, you know, playing drum and let's see who else would play piano. Sadie was playing piano. Yeah, Sadie was playing piano. I played on that. That was a nice job. I used to enjoy that, because you used to enjoy the nice ride, you know, hitting the cool, peep a nice peep. What about Cornelius? You were going to tell me about him. Oh yeah, Cornelius, yeah. Cornelius, you know when they used to tie those trucks up, you know when the band thought they were better than the other band, they wouldn't pull off, you know. But some guy would get there with the ropes, and he said, no you can't pull off, we're going to tie them all together. And Cornelius, and the bass player, I forget the bass player, the other big was wallpaper. I think it was wallpaper. But I only got the organ, you know. And Cornelius took his guitar and hit the back of it like that, and when he hit the wallpaper, his head went through the guitar, see. Well, naturally the guitar broke, and his head got caught in there, you know. And the funniest thing is he could hear you're pulling through. And those guys laughed out a week, laughed a week about that. It didn't hurt him, man, though. Yeah, it didn't hurt him. I mean, how funny it was, you know. He hit it with the guitar, and it went down his head, you know. And then they locked his head in there, you know. When they had he couldn't see the man, he was pulling, you know. Shoved him off from there and pulled him like that, you know. And those guys, man, had some fun. Buddy Petit, get it in there.
